notes: Units were aligned by position of the anchor in the source text, then checked by hand (a few adjacent-sentence mismatches were re-paired). Main disagreements: (1) actor and phase on explanatory or category-description sentences (coder A often used admin/general, coder B instructor/before-course); resolved by who the sentence addresses (instructors writing a policy, students for example syllabus text, all for facts). (2) unit_stance 'require' (B) vs 'permit' (A) on disclosure duties inside permissive example policies; resolved as permit, since the codebook reserves require for AI use being required. (3) modality must vs informs for consequence statements ('will be penalized', 'will be considered a breach'); resolved as informs. (4) policy_type splits: P66 vs P09 vs P41 on explain-your-policy advice (P66), P07 vs P61 on embedded AI (P07), P36 vs P19 on plagiarizing with AI (P36), P63 vs P85 on the College of Arts and Sciences framework (P63), P70 vs P53 on AI ethics teaching (P70), P99 vs P66 on student buy-in (P99), P40 vs P35 on baseline writing sample (P35), and P80 vs P81 on the report form (P81). One two-rule sentence (encouragement plus benefit) was split into P02 and P87 units. Single-coder units were all checked against the source and kept except two: a B heading unit duplicating an A unit (explain the why) and an A rationale sentence merged into the syllabus-explanation rule (its fit note kept). Stance was delegates for both documents in both codings. matched counts every aligned pair including those with differing codes; shares are over the 118 matched units.
